:::{#exm-log-recip}
#### The logarithm of $\frac{1}{e}$

$$
\ba
\logf{\frac{1}{e}}
&= -\logf{e}
&& \text{(logarithm of a reciprocal)}
\\
&= -1
&& \text{(} \logf{e} = 1 \text{)}
\ea
$$

The first step applies [the logarithm of a reciprocal](#cor-log-recip),
and the second uses $\logf{e} = 1$ from @exm-natural-log.

The graph of $\logf{\frac{1}{x}}$ is the graph of $\logf{x}$
reflected across the horizontal axis.
The dots mark $(e, 1)$ on the graph of $\logf{x}$
and $(e, -1)$ on the graph of $\logf{\frac{1}{x}}$.

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| echo: !expr knitr::is_html_output()
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Two curves for x from 0.1 to 5. The solid curve, the natural logarithm
#|   of x, rises from below the horizontal axis, crosses it at x = 1 and
#|   passes through a dot at (e, 1). The dashed curve, the natural logarithm
#|   of 1 over x, is its mirror image across the horizontal axis: it falls,
#|   crosses the axis at x = 1 and passes through a dot at (e, -1).

x <- seq(0.1, 5, length.out = 200)
log_x <- log(x)
reciprocal <- 1 / x
log_reciprocal <- log(reciprocal)
log_curve <- tibble::tibble(x = x, y = log_x, curve = "log(x)")
reciprocal_curve <- tibble::tibble(
  x = x, y = log_reciprocal, curve = "log(1/x)"
)
curves <- dplyr::bind_rows(log_curve, reciprocal_curve)

e_value <- exp(1)
marked_y <- c(1, -1)
marked_curve <- c("log(x)", "log(1/x)")
marked <- tibble::tibble(x = e_value, y = marked_y, curve = marked_curve)
line_types <- c("log(x)" = "solid", "log(1/x)" = "dashed")

recip_plot <- curves |>
  ggplot2::ggplot() +
  ggplot2::aes(x = x, y = y, linetype = curve) +
  ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") +
  ggplot2::geom_line() +
  ggplot2::geom_point(data = marked, colour = "firebrick", size = 2) +
  ggplot2::scale_linetype_manual(values = line_types) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "x", y = "value", linetype = NULL)

recip_plot
```

:::
